text:
Happy Halloween! The clouds have been stubborn this afternoon, so sunset around 5:43 will be a gray one with no big color show. For trick-or-treating, plan on low 40s and a light breeze. Bring a jacket and maybe a hat, but you won't need an umbrella.

Skies should thin out after dark, and we cool off to around 33 by morning. The forecasters think the cold start could end up a touch milder than some guidance says, but I'd still expect a little frost on the windshield.

Turn your clocks back an hour before bed. Sunday looks like the nicer half of the weekend: sunny, a light south breeze, and a high near 57, a solid 10 degrees warmer than today. The models all agree, so I'm confident. The mild stretch continues Monday and Tuesday, with highs from the upper 50s to low 60s. Sunday afternoon is the one to get outside for.

week.blurb: Mostly cloudy and chilly this Halloween afternoon, a high near 47, then down to about 33 tonight, so bundle up the trick-or-treaters.
Sunny and milder Sunday, a high near 57 and dry all day, a good one to get outside.
Partly sunny and mild Monday, a high near 62 and dry, a touch warmer than Sunday.
Looks like clouds build with a shower possible after 1, then a better chance after dark; high near 61.
Likely the warmest day of the week, partly sunny with a high near 65 after a stray early shower, and more showers after midnight.
Showers possible by day with a high near 64, then rain turns likely Thursday night, so keep the umbrella handy.
Trending wetter and cooler Friday, showers likely with a high near 58, and a chance they linger into the night.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Temperatures today are running just a little below seasonal norms for Halloween, with chilly 850 millibar temperatures in the -4 to -6 Celsius range close to where a subsidence inversion is present east of a ridge of high pressure. This is where our shallow clouds are, and the prevalence of stratocumulus this afternoon has been much more widespread than modeled. In turn, maximum temperatures are going to underachieve a bit in many areas with highs mainly in the low to mid 40s. That said, this should have little bearing on tonight's temperatures. In fact, have noted the National Blend of Models (NBM) looks perhaps too cold with influence of recent warm bias correction during a dry and calm pattern. Have nudged temperatures a touch warmer noting some lingering breezes and position of high pressure south of the region rather than overhead, but otherwise clearing skies and decoupling in most locations should result in a cold start to November. Thereafter, nearly continuous warm air advection is expected from the west and southwest, leading to above normal temperatures Sunday through Tuesday. Through this period, the warmest air will remain to our west so we're not looking at anything unusually warm. Any potential rain will be tied to the trajectory of a feed of deep moisture/decaying Atmospheric River entering the southwestern US tonight. Some of the moisture will rapidly push northeastward as a deep trough lifts across the Rockies and a Colorado low forms tomorrow night. The storm track will be quite amplified/stay well to our west through midweek and anomalous moisture stays to our north. Trends have continued to suggest that the polar jet gets absorbed into this system by Tuesday morning while high pressure builds back over our region following slightly enhanced gradient flow on Monday. However, frontal forcing for light rain may make its closest approach Tuesday afternoon, as some low level moisture gets pulled northward around the ridge of high pressure centered over the western mid-Atlantic region to support increasing rain chances. In any case, where clouds wind up being thick and persistent, temperatures will end up being a bit lower than currently forecast. Greatest chances of the cooler/cloudier scenario is over the northern St. Lawrence Valley, and secondarily across north central/northeastern Vermont and the remainder of northern New York. Otherwise, most likely highs both Monday and Tuesday will be about 10 to 15 degrees above normal in the upper 50s to mid 60s. KEY MESSAGE 2: The next significant weather maker will be a large trough / cold front late next week. Models are coming into agreement that the trough will come off the Rocky Mountains on Tuesday or Wednesday and begin to develop into a large area of low pressure over the Plains. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Halloween! Today will be a bit chilly, unfortunately, but otherwise it looks good for trick-or-treating. The morning will be mostly sunny, then the afternoon will turn partly sunny before becoming mainly clear again for the evening. Highs will be in the mid to upper 40s. For trick-or-treat time, temperatures will be generally in the low to mid-40s depending on what time you head out. You’ll definitely want a jacket, but thankfully the wind will be light. Sunday will be mostly sunny and warmer with highs in the 50s. The fire risk will remain elevated, but it has been reduced a bit due to the light showers from Thursday night. A reminder that we’re back to Standard Time Sunday at 2 AM. Remember to turn your clocks back 1 hour before bedtime Saturday night. The first week of November will feature some pretty nice temperatures. Monday will be partly sunny with pleasant highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. Lows will be relatively mild in the 40s. Election Day will be mostly cloudy but otherwise pleasant with highs back in the mid-50s to low 60s. A few spots could reach the mid-60s on Wednesday. The next chance for showers will be Thursday. This could be one of the wetter days we’ve had in quite some time, but models differ with the placement of the storm system. Friday will have a return to dry conditions with cooler but seasonable highs in the mid-50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-31T11:52:00Z — same caveat): Sun mixes with clouds, but chilly for Halloween — Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with highs in the mid to upper 40s and a light northwest breeze. Tonight will feature a mostly clear sky, and it turns colder. Lows reach the 20s to around 30 for most. A few high elevation towns may dip back to the teens. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the upper 50s, as a light south breeze develops. High pressure brings a mostly sunny sky through the day. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday and Tuesday look to bring more clouds than sun, with mid-60s for highs. Wednesday looks to be the warmest and brightest day. Highs will be near 70, with a gusty south breeze and partly sunny skies. Clouds thicken up Thursday, followed by a chance for substantial rain on Friday, as an area of low pressure approaches from the southwest.
